slides.title: Creating & Optimising Content for AI
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI
slides.subtitle: AMRIZE CONTENT WORKSHOP - PART 2 - 23 SEPTEMBER 2026

slides.body:
**June 17 and 25:** We built the Authority, Consistency and Relevance (ACR) framework and mapped Amrize as the master entity, with satellite entities (people, products, plants, locations) feeding it.
**The gap we're closing today:** entity mapping tells you what the network should look like. It doesn't write a single sentence. Today is about the craft of the sentences, headings and structure that make a page legible to an AI system.
**Four articles are already in motion** using these techniques, so we'll open them up as live examples, not hypotheticals.

slides.title: Why this matters more than it did a year ago
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI

slides.body:
**AEO (Answer Engine Optimization):** technical, backend, fast. Schema, structured Q&A, clean metadata. Can be implemented in weeks.
**GEO (Generative Engine Optimization):** slower and harder. Long term entity authority, third party mentions, earned media, building the reputation an LLM trusts.
**SXO:** the umbrella. Every optimisation still has to earn and convert a real site visit, not just a citation.
**Where Amrize sits today:** heavily indexed to parent Holcim/Wholesim in training data. The June 2025 launch is an opportunity to build for AI from scratch rather than retrofit.

slides.title: How to write for AI answer engines
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI

cards.body: State the citable fact or answer in the first sentence. Don't build up to it, LLMs weight early content more heavily.
cards.title: Lead with the claim

cards.body: "According to Amrize's 2026 data..." reads as more trustworthy to a model than an unattributed claim.
cards.title: Name the source explicitly

cards.body: Numbered lists and stats near the top reduce the computational cost for an LLM to extract and quote you.
cards.title: Frontload numbered evidence

cards.body: Subheadings phrased as questions, answered directly underneath, mirror how RAG systems retrieve passages.
cards.title: Use explicit Q&A structure

cards.body: LLMs actively discount thin, templated, obviously automated prose. Human centric content outperforms it 2 to 3x.

slides.title: How we structure an AEO optimised article
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI

stages.name: Answer first
stages.caption: Open with the direct, citable answer to the implied question. No throat clearing.

stages.name: Evidence block
stages.caption: Numbered facts, named sources, dates, frontloaded immediately after the claim.

stages.name: Entity reinforcement
stages.caption: Name people, products, locations exactly as they appear in the entity map, every time.

stages.name: Q&A subheadings
stages.caption: Break the body into explicit question and answer sections for RAG retrieval.

stages.name: Schema tagging
stages.caption: Apply Schema.org markup so crawlers and LLMs parse structure correctly.

slides.body:
**AIO (AI assisted operations) is useful for:** repetitive technical metadata, schema generation, formatting consistency, tasks that don't require judgement.
**AIO does not, on its own, increase your AI visibility score.** It removes friction; it doesn't create authority.

slides.title: Where automation helps, and where it hurts
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI
slides.subtitle: AI can do the plumbing. It cannot do the judgement.
slides.bodyRight:
**The trap to avoid:** LLMs actively discount thin, templated prose that reads as purely machine generated. Volume without distinct expertise or voice is invisible, not just ignored.
**The Amrize opportunity:** named technical voices such as plant managers, engineers and technical specialists are entity signals a generic corporate voice can never be.

slides.title: Practising it yourselves
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI

slides.body:
**Pick a page:** a case study, product page or bio you're responsible for.
**Rewrite the opening:** lead with the citable claim, name the source, add one frontloaded fact.
**Add one Q&A subheading:** phrase it exactly as a customer or AI system would ask it.
**Swap and critique:** in pairs, check whether the rewrite would survive being quoted out of context by an AI answer. Does it still make sense and still name Amrize?

slides.title: What good looks like: a before and after
slides.footer: The Content Engine · Amrize Content Workshop: Creating & Optimising Content for AI
slides.bodyRight: "Amrize supplies ready mix concrete to the Denver dam rehabilitation project, one of several major U.S. infrastructure projects the company has completed since its June 2025 launch. [Named engineer], Amrize's [title], led the technical specification."

slides.body:
**Does the first sentence answer a real question a customer or AI system would ask?**
**Is at least one claim attributed to a named, specific source?**
**Are people, products and locations named exactly as they appear in the entity map?**
**Is there at least one explicit Q&A subheading?**
**Would this survive being quoted alone, out of context, by an AI answer?**
**Has schema/structured data been applied before publishing?**
